extracted.intended_audience: educators, coaches, mentors, and practitioners engaged with open science who support early career researchers, undergraduates, graduate students, journal clubs, or review club members
extracted.subtask_short: platform design for instructional peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating features, workflows, and materials that make an open preprint peer-review platform (PREreview) useful for teaching and training in a variety of educational settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make open peer review more accessible, inclusive, and helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of our mission at PREreview to make open peer review more accessible, inclusive, and helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design decisions should prioritize accessibility (lowering barriers to participation), inclusivity (welcoming diverse learners and reviewers), and practical helpfulness for both authors and learners. The platform should serve authors improving their work and students/early-career researchers learning review skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaffolded and welcoming reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: These efforts are meant to make reviewing on PREreview as scaffolded and welcoming as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scaffolding (step-by-step supports, prompts) and a welcoming user experience so beginners feel comfortable participating. Anti-pattern: leaving novice reviewers without structure or guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured review workflows that model reviewer questions
rubrics_metrics.description: We have developed features like 'structured review' workflows to model the kinds of questions we hope our reviewers will answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured workflows to exemplify the types of questions and evaluation steps instructors want learners to practice. Examples: templated prompts or sections that guide attention to methods, clarity, novelty, or ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide review guides and training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: We also share multiple review guides and training materials on our website and through Zenodo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and surface pedagogical materials (guides, tutorials, example reviews) that instructors can reuse in classroom or lab settings. Guidance includes hosting, citing, and linking to reusable resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help educators teach the hows and whys of open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: We can do more to help coaches, educators, and mentors teaching early career researchers, undergrads, and grad students the hows and whys of open peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design features and materials that explicitly support pedagogy: learning objectives, exercises, discussion prompts, and explanations of rationale behind review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be useful across different educational settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Discover what teachers and learners need from PREreview to make it more useful for instructional use across different educational settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure flexibility to accommodate classrooms, labs, journal clubs, review clubs, and varied curricula. Solicit input from diverse instructors to identify missing features or adaptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support development of critical-thinking, writing, and ethical review skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Open preprint review is invaluable ... for early career researchers to train their critical-thinking and writing skills, to learn how to perform rigorous, ethical peer review, and to improve how they plan, undertake, document, and communicate their own research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform design and materials should aim to foster these specific learning outcomes (critical analysis, constructive writing, ethical standards, research communication). Include examples and exercises targeted at these competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate participation by offering multiple session times
rubrics_metrics.description: To make sure that as many people as possible can participate, we'll facilitate two design sprints at different times on different weekdays. You only need to attend one call to share your input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule events and synchronous activities at varied times to accommodate different time zones and availability. Offer single-attendance options so contributors need not join multiple sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer modest honorarium to significant contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer a modest honorarium to any participant who contributes significantly to a call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide compensation where appropriate to recognize contributors' time and expertise. Define 'contributes significantly' and the process to request/receive the honorarium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit recording and AI use; prioritize human interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not record or use AI if you join a call. We invite and celebrate human interaction and feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt policies that protect participants' comfort and privacy: forbid session recording and generative-AI use during calls to encourage candid, human-to-human discussion. Explain rationale and enforce norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain communication and community channels for ongoing engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have something to share, drop us an email at help@prereview.org. You can follow us on Mastodon, BlueSky, LinkedIn, and YouTube. You can also keep up with all the latest news by subscribing to our newsletter and joining our Slack community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multiple, discoverable channels (email, social platforms, newsletter, Slack) so educators and practitioners can stay engaged, share feedback, and access resources. Ensure links and subscription mechanisms are up to date.
